page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Motion in a Straight Line · 2 marks

steps.label: Distance
lines: Distance is the total length of the path
actually travelled. It is a scalar and can
never be negative or zero for a moving body.
steps.why: Distance adds up every part of the journey regardless of direction, so it only ever grows.
common_mistakes: Calling distance a vector. It has magnitude only.

recall.must_convey: That distance is the length of the path travelled and is a scalar.

steps.memory_tip: Distance is what the odometer reads. It only goes up.
steps.margin_note: Say "scalar" — it is half of the contrast.

steps.label: Displacement

lines.text: Displacement is the change in position

lines: measured in a straight line from start to
finish. It is a vector, and it is zero for any
round trip that returns to the start.
steps.why: Displacement depends only on the two end points, so a body that returns to where it began has zero displacement however far it walked.
common_mistakes: Saying displacement can never be zero for a moving body. A round trip gives exactly zero.

recall.must_convey: That displacement is the straight-line change in position, is a vector, and is zero for a round trip.

steps.memory_tip: Displacement uses only the two end points. A round trip gives zero.
steps.margin_note: The round-trip case is the sharpest contrast.

insider_note: Two marks means two contrasts. Scalar against vector, and path length against straight-line change.
